determinism.method: The fill runner was executed twice, independently, and the full exercise log (all 30 member->key->identity_space triples with their predicate verdicts) was captured from each run and byte-compared. A negative control was then run on the comparison instrument itself: a planted single-token difference was introduced into a copy of run 1 and the same diff was re-run, to establish that the instrument can SEE a difference when one exists -- a diff that is blind returns 'identical' for a stable run and an unstable one alike.
determinism.observed: STABLE. Two runs produced byte-identical 169-line exercise logs. The instrument negative control reported the planted difference, so the STABLE verdict is attributable rather than an artifact of a blind comparison. NOTE ON SCOPE: this measures determinism of the KEY EXPRESSIONS and their exercises, which is the property the criteria turn on. The full written payload is NOT byte-stable across runs because the evidence appendix embeds the run's UTC timestamp; that is by design and is stated rather than smoothed over.

surprises: ⛔ A CORRECTION MADE INSIDE THIS FILL, on W3-thav, recorded because the WRONG read was the plausible one and it survived a control. Counting ARN coverage with `count(n.arn)` returned 27054 of 27054 non-null and I concluded the `node.get('arn') or node.get('id')` fallback branch was UNREACHED in the live population. It counts EMPTY STRINGS. Corrected denominator: arn IS NULL = 0, arn = '' = 25197, arn non-empty = 1857. The empty string is FALSY in Python, so the fallback carries 93.1% of the population -- the OPPOSITE conclusion. The wrong number was internally consistent and would have been written onto a delivered card as a measured finding. The discriminating instrument was asking for a member of the supposedly-empty set and reading what came back (arn was ''), not re-running the count.

⛔ THE B1 DELTA-PASS SENTENCE GOES FALSE ON EVERY CARD THIS FILL RAISES, AND NOTHING WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT. The migrator appended '|| v3 delta pass: key_expression ABSENT on this card (not yet declared by the carding lane); row basis lowered from measured to the floor' to trust.key.evidence. On the 8 rows the fill raises to 'measured' that sentence now sits in the SAME FIELD as the value that falsifies it. No validator reads prose, so a card can be schema-valid and self-contradictory at once. Handled by DISCHARGING it by name in the appended evidence and RETAINING it as the record of the migration. This affects every lane's fill, not just mine -- 72 cards went through the same delta pass. Routed as an OBSERVATION.

⛔ OBSERVATION (inert): edge_grain_binding carries NINE keys, not eight. `S3Key`, the sole key under the `partition` group, is a NODE type and not an edge_type. A consumer enumerating the block's keys to build a D1-bound edge-type list picks up one literal that can never match an edge, and the miss is silent because a no-match edge_type query returns 0 rows identically to a correct query over an empty set. W2-kwjy's expression now names the 8-key member set explicitly.

⛔ OBSERVATION (inert): W2-dmua's and W2-qgtd's identity_space PROSE under-describes their own key space, in a direction that breaks a join. W2-dmua's says 'artifact filenames including templated ones ({date}.json ...)' where the actual keys are FULL artifact:s3:// URIs; 3 of the 7 keys are templates and match a SET rather than a member. W2-qgtd's names bare quantities ('advisor_intelligence') where the actual contract_id is '<quantity>-<surface-family>' with the quantity segment HYPHENATED ('advisor-intelligence-nna') -- a consumer joining on the bare underscored name misses on both counts. Recorded in the key rows' evidence; identity_space itself was NOT edited, because AC5 confines the diff to the key rows.

Routed through .tools/msys_argv_guard.py msys_safe_run per CLAUDE.md's Git section. Noted because the failure mode is a spawn error rather than a wrong answer, so it is loud -- but a runner that wrapped the spawn in a bare except would have converted it into a silent zero.
